items.title: Netflix at QConSF 2026: Retrofitting the SDLC for AI Coding Agents
items.summary: At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mark Khuzam of Netflix explained how the Commerce team retrofitted its SDLC so AI coding agents and engineers could ship together. The team wrote 45 architecture decision records for people and agents, added a review agent that posts only verified blockers, and serves per-domain GraphRAG context through a single MCP tool. By Andrew Hoblitzell

items.title: Review: The Asus ProArt P16 offers a glimpse of a future powered by local AI
items.summary: The new Asus ProArt laptop costs up to $7,000, but it can run a gaggle of local AI agents.

items.title: Podcast: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
items.summary: Michael Stiefel spoke to Zhou Yu about using dynamic simulations to evaluate AI agents. One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks. You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases. By Zhou Yu

items.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Harness Is the New Operating System
items.summary: At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mad Labs founder and CEO Manju Rajashekhar opened the conference arguing that the harness around an AI model, rather than the model itself, decides what an agent can do and how safely it does it. The keynote mapped the parts of a harness, including context, tools, state, permissions and feedback loops, onto jobs that operating systems already perform. By Andrew Hoblitzell
